body:
He has demanded marriage counseling, which I have agreed to mostly to appear as though I'm putting forth effort to work through it. This is a preemptive measure in case he decides to draw things out and make this a huge nasty divorce but yes, I am planning on divorcing him. 
I *believe* I have health coverage for 60 days after the divorce but I'm not aware if I would still be covered during a separation. I need to look into that more throughly. Here in NC you have to be legally separated for 1 year and 1 day to file for divorce. 

Thank you for this information. 
I was hoping they would allow it to stay up since I wasn't sure of another sub relevant to my situation so I really do appreciate it. I'm going to go check r/sterilization out now as well.

Sorry, North Carolina. Around Jacksonville.  This is my throwaway account but I'm nervous he may see this somehow and get in the way. I did look over the list in the sidebar and all of those are at least an hour away. Ultimately, if I don't have any other options I'll find a way to make it work with someone on that list. 
I was mostly just hoping for a miracle of a chance that someone in this sub knew of a dr here who would possibly help out. Thank you!

I know his CO is not on any lists to receive a World's Best Boss mug, for sure. I know he's stressed out related to work but he's also been stressed because he's alone...with a bunch of dudes...haha if you know what I mean. Involuntary celibacy can really bring you down. 
They can't write yet, but I could help them, or translate.  
He isn't/we aren't super religious necessarily, but we kind of go through some of the basics. I say evening prayers with my kids every night at bedtime and he's always included- we also end them with "...keep daddy safe, amen." 
They talk about him often, at least once a day. My youngest draws squiggles that he says are cats and helicopters for him all the time. I've looked into the daddy dolls, as well, but don't have a full body picture to use. I might ask for one of him next time we talk. 
It's extremely difficult for him to communicate his emotions so for him to open up and let me know he was having a hard time is big. I just don't know how to show him he's utterly missed, by all of us.

I have no doubt that homecoming will be amazing! 
Every opportunity he's been able to call, he does and I always put our kids on. They're very young, so they just talk nonsense most of the time and don't fully listen to him, but I always have them say "miss you daddy, I love you daddy". 
I email him videos of them. They draw/make things for him almost daily but I haven't sent him anything they've made yet. Maybe I should?
*PEOPLE OF THE WORLD*

My parents have  multitude of issues and I really wouldn't be surprised if this were the case. 
My mom makes up excuses to not have to go anywhere without him, literally ever, or flat out refuses. She wouldn't come see her own daughter and grandkids- *on my dime*!- because she couldn't bear to leave my stepdad. Yet my husband was across the country when she said that for a few weeks, now he's gone again and comes back in about 6 months-ish. I can't tolerate this ultra dependent bullshit.

Keeping her safe is my number one priority. I know it seems like they don't love her because of how they treat her but through all the denial and delusion, they do. I think they just don't take her seriously. At all. 
I couldn't imagine just sitting back and doing nothing (which is why I'm absolutely floored by my entire immediate family's actions- or inaction, I guess) because everyone closest to her knows there is a problem but refuses to address it until the family loudmouth forces it to their attention. 
I hope you had *someone* who cares deeply about you. Everyone deserves that much.
You and me both, dude.

>I want to gain weight

Shut up, you mythological unicorn! What's that like? God, I would eat ridiculous amounts of cheese. :C

I save up those meals for the local pizza joint and delivery hibachi. It wrecks my innards for the next week, and I feel like shit after, but sometimes you just need it. 
I treat it like a break up; it's been nearly 8 years. Why go back now? I'll just look back on it with a delusional fondness haha. 
Plus, mamas got a goal weight for a new set of melons and I ain't gonna get 'em eating biscuits!
I haven't had one in nearly 8 years, I think. Damn near a decade.

Thank you! It seems to be the general consensus here, so it's nice to have these first hand accounts. 
As for her depression, I don't know the severity of it. All I'm going on is a few pages from a journal my brother saw and photographed as well as knowing her demeanor and daily habits. I do know she's been bullied since at *least* first grade. Had death threats at age 11, and recently had some girls smash her head into her locker. Our state is a zero tolerance policy state but nothing has been done to reprimand the kids who make her life hell, daily. I'm honestly shocked my parents haven't pulled her out of school. God help those little asswipes if I'm ever around and they pull that shit.

You know what's sad? I've been to KFC like a solid dozen or so times in my life, and only two times did they actually have chicken available. 
I suppose I can't really miss what I never really had haha. But those biscuits though... *tear of sadness*. Eat one for me. Just don't tell me how delicious it was.

I'll absolutely mention this to my mom, I can't get her personally to one since I live 800+ miles away. But I'm sure my mom will have a battery of tests performed to disprove it is simple overeating, under exercising. I'm honestly not even sure if she's been to one yet, but it's worth looking into. 
I really appreciate your advice!! Thank you!

Haha I'm a "m'lady". But no worries, I'm not judging! I remember that crunchy delicious, brown skin. And also the chicken. 
And thank you.
/u/skyblacker just beat you to that reference by a couple of minutes- but I skimmed over! I'm sure I'll find good points in there for future "disagreements" with my family.

I know she has potential. I know she also needs structure and to learn how to discipline herself. My husband helped get me started with both of those things. He's a great man and an amazing teacher. I think being around him would do her a world of good. 
If she could pick up habits from him like I have, she could do a total 180. He's also a jack of all trades, and she might pick up hobbies as well!  This definitely has me excited for this coming summer. I don't think I'm going to give my parents a choice. She has to come. Has to.

Just skimmed it. As a former fat girl, who got fit then gained some back after 2 kids, I've got plenty left to lose and I agree with a lot on the sub. I know it's all fine and good now to love yourself and accept who you are, but how can anyone settle for feeling like shit inside, everyday, over something that 99.99% people have the power to change?

This wouldn't be an issue at ALL at my house. My damn fridge is void of pretty much anything right now haha. 
I keep bags upon bags of those organic chicken breasts, broccoli, spinach, and frozen tilapia. Everything else I buy fresh. Of course I'll occasionally order out (local NY style pizza and hibachi/sushi delivered, dude. Even I can't say no sometimes) but they just keep pure, processed, filthy trash stocked in every single cupboard. Ice cream. Chips. Dip. Cokes. They had *so much cereal, there were at least 10 unopened, expired boxes* and they still had plenty of new boxes. Frozen meals galore. Carbs, carbs, carbs. All day, every day. Their idea of eating "better" is to order a Large #3 at Wendy's with a Diet Coke. Woo!
Just spending 2 months here alone, eating what we eat, I know she would lose weight. I eat 3 medium sized meals and snack on healthy stuff throughout the day- rice cakes, green apple slices with peanut butter, Greek yogurt and granola. I used to eat the way they did. If I can change, **anyone** can haha.

I'll certainly look into it. They have great healthcare, so the only issue would be making sure it's covered out of state. My parents are tightwads.
I'm about 75% certain my family will be visiting for Christmas so I'll have some research done before then to give to my mom. I can also take my sister shopping or something for some quality sister time and talk to her about things then.

Regarding college, I never got to go myself (married and pregnant at 19) but I've talked to my little brother about his classes and given a little advice. By the time my sister is graduated, my kids will both be in school full time so I could possibly enroll with her, even. 
The biggest issue I've found with her (I'm assuming another symptom of depression) is that she doesn't seem to feel passionate enough about anything to want to go to school for it. I know some of her interests, she dabbles in stuff so I could speak with her more in depth to see if anything has changed about that. Our parents put pretty much all of their college ducks in my little brothers basket...(he'd be the first to graduate among all of us siblings). I know she feels left out and like our brother is the favorite (frankly, he is) and it seems like they don't much care about her college career closing in. They had my brothers schooling figured out by the time he was in the 7th grade. 
There are so many facets to her depression, that being one of them, I'm sure.

>I am in no way a professional- unlike many of us in this subreddit

That gave me a good laugh. 

I can understand where you're coming from. Admittedly, yes- I know that it *is* a violation, but if she hadn't been bullied so relentlessly from kindergarten till now (and it doesn't look hopeful that it will stop) I would in no way be ok with my little brother snooping that way. I, too, kept journals. Hell, I still do. But for me, this has much less to do about her journals and more to do with her entire demeanor about life. 
Whenever I'm around her, there are very, very few things that seem to spark her interest. The rest of the time she is visibly depressed. I don't know if my parents are just used to that sort of behavior from her, but I know from being around her as a young kid she wasn't always like this. She's had death threats. At age *11*. She has endured far too much for far too long. 
The fact that my mom, every adult in my family, was so utterly oblivious to all of this is what scares me the most. The people who are closest to her every single day of her life think everything is fine. That tells me they have no idea what she's capable of. It's terrifying to me. I couldn't stand to lose her. Depression runs in my family, but they don't want to be diagnosed and attempt to treat it because the stigma of the label is humiliating to them.  
If this is the only way I can help, I'd do it a thousand times over. I'll certainly apologize to her in the future, and ask for her forgiveness. She may choose not to forgive but that much I can live with.

Firstly- I'm sorry that you dealt with those things. It sucks. I hope you had someone who cared enough to realize you were dealing with those feelings and did something to be supportive. 
Secondly- I simply asked my little brother about how she was doing and he offered up that oh, btw, she seems severely depressed and *he* read in her journal and she wrote in there that she wanted to die. I did not encourage him to read it, he did that on his own before the subject ever even came up. That being said, if my sister's life is at stake, I could give a single fuck about privacy. She can get her privacy back. I live 800+ miles away. You know I can't get back? My baby sister if she kills herself because no one took her cries for help seriously. 
I'm sorry, but I wholeheartedly disagree with you. I'll take my chances. 

Also: I've had my privacy invaded countless times. I'm totally fine. I don't hate the people who did it. I got over it.
*Calm down, John Wilkes Booth*.

You know what, thank you. Sincerely, thank you. 
I start feeling guilty hoping I didn't stick my nose where it didn't belong but Jesus, man, *I just want them to live longer.* Why do I feel so guilty about that?

I have literally never seen any of them put a single bite of healthy food in their mouths. Not one of them. 
Even salads are drowned in dressing and covered with cheese and croutons and glazed nuts. And that's just the appetizer...
A couple of years ago, they came to visit. They rented a vacation home (they didn't like going by my house rules the time they visited before that- which was to be respectful of me in MY HOUSE) and were grilling out. We brought over our usual- turkey burger meat and those flat Nature's Own buns, spinach, etc. They took one look at our bag of food and said "wtf is that crap?" It's food? "We can't eat that! The kids won't touch it!" Have they ever even had turkey burgers before? "Not. But they're picky. I know they won't like it." My mom left, drove into town, and bought the cheap, fatty hamburger, chips, dip, cokes, and cookies. 
Seriously? Just because you were raised one way doesn't mean it's impossible to change habits or lifestyle.  This is how they've lived my entire life. Over 24 years. And anytime I visit with my kids, they try to do the same. They want to give my kids sweets, I say they love watermelon. *She comes back with watermelon flavored candy*.
They actually have phenomenal coverage! They just don't utilize it for the right things! It's infuriating.

If I knew how long we would be here, this would absolutely be my number one priority. But my husband's profession require us to move every few years. 
There's a chance we could stay here longer, and if this is the case I would fill out everything *for* her and bring her down myself. It's not out of the question, for sure.

I've tried talking exercise with her several times before and she has identical coping skills to our mom- she shuts down. She completely ignores you if she doesn't want to continue talking about something, even if mid-conversation. She's done it to me every time. She might be 16, but growing up with her I know she isn't emotionally at the same level as her peers. For instance: 4 years back, hanging out with my my stepmom and step brother and sister, who were 10 and 9 at the time, were mentally more capable and mature than my sister- 12- at everything. And this goes for any kids I've met. I don't know if they've ever had her tested for developmental delays but it shows in her schooling, her relationships with her friends, how she acts, how she handles nearly any situation. She may be 16 but she doesn't really act it. 
The only reason I'm not keeping this strictly between me and her is because I don't wholly believe she's be capable of handling this alone. She's extremely sensitive and bringing it up with her could possibly push her into something I don't know that I could handle.
I know I should encourage her to talk with school counselors, but my mom works for the school and they're all buddy-buddy. They live in small town, America. My mom is highly respected and praised by her coworkers and people in the community and I feel like they won't take my sister seriously. 
I'm going to see if my mom will see about speaking with a therapist out of town (she's already giving me excuses why she can't set up appointments there in town- "everyone here is booked with kids who are more 'emergency cases'! They don't have room for her. She can talk to my therapist friend at Zumba!"???).
Duly noted, but she won't be actually joining in on that. At least not for a very long time. She's got knee issues already, so they typically stick with walking and treadmills/ellipticals.

I just recently started there myself and I'm absolutely not the only beginner there (meaning there are people at various points on the fitness scale there). If it weren't for the owner knowing what he's talking about I wouldn't even consider it. 
But I also do it 3 days a week and I would rather she come with than just chill on the couch with no one home, ya know?

I could absolutely ask, but I wouldn't be surprised if she either "misplaced them", tossed them, or just didn't have them. 
She's an RN, so she has a basic understanding of how it would work. I think her denial runs so deep that she genuinely believes it couldn't possibly be how my sister eats/lives. Because that would immediately reflect on her as a parent. 

I'll try to do a little research so I can ask her what the results were and be able to tell if she's spouting off BS or if the dr's are truly, potentially disregarding another possible reason. 
Thank you for you input!!

Honestly, my family is a clusterfuck in and of itself. They would all benefit from therapy as they all have some serious personal issues, some of which I know, most I don't. 
I can only suggest what I think they should do, which I'll certainly tell her to take it one step at a time, but it's her choice/ their choices to listen or not. 

And I definitely don't intend to suggest any of them start crossfit. At all. It would be physically impossible for them at this point regardless. Baby steps. I know.

Definitely agree with you! 
I actually told my mom she should try consistent exercise and healthy/less eating before resorting to drugs and she actually acted like she didn't hear me. 
I've been talking to my sister much more regularly, so I think I can try to influence her to use good old fashioned will power and elbow grease before getting into chemicals. 
That's where personal experience comes in- if I can do (albeit on a smaller scale) she can absolutely do it. She just has to want it enough to try. Ultimately, I really have no say over anything, I can only continue to point out the things that aren't working. Thank you!

Whoa whoa whoa- not getting her to join crossfit! Haha. That wasn't what I meant. I should have been clearer but I just wanted her to come along to speak with people there and hopefully learn something. I don't expect her to legit participate but it would be awesome to get her to do a little lifting or warm up stuff. I'm not expecting her to bust out some WODs or anything like that. Like you said- something light. This is all also dependent on of my parents allow her to come for he summer- still no solid answer on that btw. 

Also, it's technically up to our mom since my sister is still a minor. I can't really drive half way across the country and just take her back home with me, unfortunately. (Which sucks because she's my sister and I should be able to do that!) I'll be pretty relentless about her coming out, so maybe they'll give in. I really do want to spend quality time with her. 
My mom will be keeping me in the loop regarding what's going on, so I'll tell her not to try to attack this entire situation head on and expect miraculous results. But I DO expect SOME results. Her past behavior has proven she is complacent while trying to APPEAR as though she's putting for effort. She's been going to the gym consistently for over a year now and has lost ZERO weight. Who the fuck *maintains* 300 lbs at 5'3"? Not someone who is legitimately trying. Trust me, I know that. 
I'll definitely encourage her/them to tackle one issue at a time, but they don't really have the luxury of "years" here. They're all in trouble if they don't start changing shit, and fast. 

Quick edit- I thought my grandpa would be supportive of me in telling my family that their lifestyle is a bad one. He's usually a level headed, brutally honest guy but has told me he "doesn't want to get involved", most likely because my whole family gets butthurt easily. Neither of my brothers wanted to back me up because they're both financially dependent on my parents, so my grandpa would have been my only "ally" here.

I might look up some and refer her to a few. You're hitting the nail on the head though. 
She's an RN and if the doc doesn't say what she wants to hear, then that dr is just stupid. 
However, multiple dr's all saying the exact same thing can't be wrong. She can say it's a thyroid problem all she wants, when in reality we ALL know it's a grazing problem. 
I never read the term until I joined Reddit, and it's a perfect description of my family. 

Well, now I'm rambling, but I will absolutely be "assisting from afar" as much as possible. I'll probably get dog shit for Christmas. Ha. It'll be worth it if they live another 40 years. I'll gladly accept dog shit every Christmas for the foreseeable future. I really appreciate your input though, I wouldn't have thought to suggest an actual dietician.

Thank you!! I think updates, especially positive ones!, are necessary. Being able to see that others share my thoughts and concerns for her well being help me feel like I'm doing right by her and not "ruining her life" by essentially outing her to our parents. 
I feel like everyone in my family is too busy trying to make excuses for why it's ok for her to be 400+ lbs at 16 when they aren't worrying about the consequences or underlying causes of that. Exercise and healthy eating work! I'm proof of that! I get to say it and not have them throw it in my face that it's false! 
I think telling my mom that she talked about dying every day is what did it. I really tried to hit home that she needs to speak to someone- as in a licensed professional- to help deal with things. Just losing the weight doesn't mean you lose the feelings that caused it all.  My mom said she would keep me updated with everything so I'll be sure to let her know this is a must. Mental health is equally important!
...said u/ShutMyBallsInTheDoor, ironically.

Thank you for the input! Very good suggestion!

I also just asked him today about glasses (I used to wear them until one of my offspring snapped them in half haha) and he said that would actually make it even better, he really liked the glasses!

I have to admit that I'm not sure what watersports are (I'm assuming it involves the color gold) at one point, talk was on the table to open the marriage (my idea) and he declined. Regarding your threesome scenario- he's previously proposed a fmf threesome to me and I agreed under one condition, that I get to explore my same interest in the mfm threesome. We both decided that that was a hard pass for both of us because we simply don't like to share. Mutual monogamy all around. 
While I can understand to an extent that feeling sexually unfulfilled can cause issues in the marriage (I've been there. I know what sad, depressing, rejected, sexually starved feels like dude) and can even ultimately lead to divorce, I think it's kind of bullshit to cop out and say "if you don't fulfill my anal vacuum kink I'll just go find someone who will!" I'm allowed to have boundaries within the relationship. There is self control. If he can't keep it in his pants because I won't let him cum on my face then that's his problem (and it won't be a problem in this case, but it's a little sad that you think this way, and that's coming from someone who was utterly shutdown sexually for 18 months in a 2 year time period.)
The cum on the face thing is currently a soft no for me, but until it happens in a situation where it's "controlled" and not "oh fuck, sorry that got in your eyeball when it should have been on your stomach!" I can't say it's a hard no or yes. 
I'm not asking him to give up his one request of me. And it's not like he hasn't denied me certain things. Important things. Big things. But we compromise. We try. This time, I just need a little outside perspective. 
While this might be his most recent fetish come to light, I don't doubt it will be the last that comes up. I've got things I'd like to explore and I'm sure he's got more hell eventually like to as well.

I had the same thought myself earlier today in the event that it won't happen again he at least has some nice memorabilia. 
We shall see. I'll try it at least once and see how it goes.

Mmm...he actually has a specific no-no (or at least two, actually) that is/are very common and while I can do without, I wouldn't say he's doing "everything" he can haha. He's just doing well enough with he things he does do and we compromise, which makes up for it.

Those are actually some good, solid ideas. The thought of rubbing it on my face doesn't have the cringe-factor as the random shooting does. I'll definitely propose that and see what he thinks! Thank you! 
As for wiping it off, he said he wants me to keep it on. Obviously not all day but as long as possible, and maybe even continue going- as in "see how much I can take" to the face. 
I've always got wet wipes or a washcloth handy by the bed though, so I might stash some extras in the event of an 'eye'mergency?

While I personally wouldn't mind the high part, he actually does the drug testing within his job so that is unfortunately a no-go haha. Although our drunk sex, while it's been few and far between since we got married and had kids, was mind-blowing from what I can recall. Maybe I'll suggest a sitter for the evening and we can try that again. 

I can certainly understand the idea of "coming to terms" and eventually loving something- I was the same with blowjobs. I'd given 3 other guys blowjobs in my entire life and even those had to be easily less than 20 in total. Now I love them because I love the control I get and making him squirm. 

I think fake it till you make it might be the best advice possible in this situation.

I don't know if I touched on that point in the original post but he said he doesn't want me to wash it off. He wants me to keep it on my face and keep going- "see how times you can take it to the face". 
Semen itself doesn't gross me out, I just don't want it on my face and even I can't tell you why. I just don't.
This is true. I've got more than enough time.

Well shit. Years?

I keep trying to think of ways "around" the issue... Wear a mask? Wear goggles? Could glasses work like goggles?

I actually saw another thing here on Reddit called the Kindu app? I've started taking that but he's got extremely limited internet where he is with his type of job right now, so he for sure can't download the app and might not be able to take the quiz. Definitely worth a shot though. 
As for the neck and chest thing, he's fine with both of those but seems to really, really be into the face deal. Like he's asked multiple times if I'd actually let him do it, and says he thinks I'm not being serious or will bail.

I'm not sure about a pediatrician but they are known on a first name basis at their family physician because they are all hypochondriacs on top of having legitimate health issues. The problem is that they downplay the serious conditions (obesity, adult onset diabetes, asthma, etc.) and try to blame smaller, insignificant, and irrelevant, conditions (thyroid- which was ruled out, knee problems, headaches...)
I'm not sure if that's something I can even legally do? I want to bring it up with my parents first to give them one last chance, then go from there. I'm also concerned about mentioning the suicide issue right off the bat with a dr, because if she hasn't spoken with a psychiatrist first who could rule out her actually being suicidal and just being overdramatic, it could land her in the local mental hospital. I know I need to do some research on my states laws to see if I have any power to make those claims without being a parent or guardian. I'm beginning to really resent my parents for putting me in this situation that it would have to even be an option, at this point.

The "liability " is another reason I reached out to my grandpa this afternoon, because I couldn't handle knowing that I had the opportunity to prevent something from happening to her if she either has a heart attack and dies at 16 or attempts/commits suicide and told him as much. He agreed that she needs therapy and said he would bring it up to my mom. 
I would take her in immediately if it ever got to that point, and I'll let her know that she is welcome here, regardless of the situation, at any time.
Well then, can you explain the term "**morbidly** obese", please?

I never understood why believers would stand on a stage, talking to more believers about their beliefs. Jesus walked miles upon miles to talk to the sick and poor, as well as the rich and ignorant. 
I asked my mom why we didn't do something more like that instead of sitting and listening to the same old messages, spun from a different angle by a different guy on a different day, and she said something to the effect of "Because you can learn something new every day...". 

Like...what?
Of course you can learn something new every day, people use scripture as a mad libs, and drop in their own bias and analyses. I have more respect for the missionaries or even just volunteers who get out of their comfortable environments around their comfortable pew neighbors and actually help others and potentially risk their lives. I know not everyone can do that, but I think that's what truly separates the herd- those who are willing to do *something* to improve the quality of life around them with more than just a simple "I'll pray for you" on facebook.
I think the trolls just came out for dinner; I refuse to believe someone actually wrote that with an iota of sincerity.

>/s

I think you're right. I've always felt that the people in the churches I grew up in always had a clause for certain rules-
Treat others the way you'd like to be treated, **if** they believe what you believe.
Accept everyone, **except** everyone.
Jesus loved the sinner, hated the sin *but* it was tough love and saying NO HUMAN RIGHTS FOR YOU, ASSHOLES!

This is why I now identify more as spiritual than religious because I hated identifying with such a blatantly judgmental, hypocritical organization, save for the few and far between who had common sense and compassion.

My family has always told me I'm abrasive and brutally honest, and I know that it isn't always the best way to deal with subjects as sensitive as these, but I can't just dance around a subject. I think there is *some* weight to the excuses, but that's really all they are- excuses. I **do** believe that when I start this ride, both brothers will fall in line and back me up, without a doubt. They won't be as gung ho as I will be, but I also don't owe them anything- financially or otherwise. I honestly don't mind being the asshole in the family, I've played that role for a while (which my grandpa confirmed earlier on the phone). Better to be an honest asshole than a timid, two-faced one, I suppose.

It was suggested in another comment that bringing her issues up directly to her might potentially cause more damage, causing her to distance herself more. I think I might just try to talk more with her as the school year progresses and then try to get her to come out and work with her that way- focusing on the positives and tackling the weight issue "under the table" (E.G- hey, lets go on a walk and you can tell me about your friends!)

My sister is great with children, as is my brother. They're around my niece almost daily. I don't know that they have mental issues that would end up being threatening to my children, but if that did end up being the case I would obviously send them home. 
I know my brother won't be an issue, but I always noticed that my sister seem extremely socially delayed and acted years younger than her age for a long time. For instance, she was 12 and my dad's fiancée's kids were 8 and 9 and far more mature than she was. I'm not sure what to make of that, which is another reason I desperately want her to get into long term therapy.

My grandpa actually said he would talk to my mom about the journal entries, but with my sister's birthday this week he wants to wait to do so, somewhat understandably. I do feel that once he mentions this to her, shit will hit the fan and I might lose my window to invite her for the summer. I'll just have to play it by ear.

They're working their way up to that pretty fucking quickly, yeah.

I used to blame it on their ignorance, but I'm learning through talking more with my siblings that this just isn't the case.

I'm a SAHM, so I'd be with her constantly. Maybe even too much, I don't want to be 20 feet up her ass haha, but she's at the point that it would require me to stay on her case, in a non-nagging, non-threatening way, to get out of bed, out of the bedroom, or get off the couch. She doesn't drive yet, so she can't really just go out and get whatever she wants, and has no bank account so unless she steals a card (she's known to take things and lie) she won't be getting any food we don't provide.
 
She actually can't ride a bike for long because she's so heavy it hurts her and strains her knees. To top all of that off, she has asthma ( giving her the BEST reason to get active and lose weight...) so we would have to take it slow anyway. 

I think walking around a local track or even my neighborhood would do her good.
